title: Pentakaka
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A wondrous story is told of him in the Jerusalem Talmud, Taanit chapter 1, halakha 4: in the days of Rabbi Abbahu (in Caesarea) they were in need of rain, and it was shown to Rabbi Abbahu in a dream that a certain man named Pentakaka should pray and rain would fall. He sent for him and asked him what his deeds were, and he told him that he commits four transgressions every day: he hires out prostitutes, he adorns a place of entertainment, he brings the garments for the prostitutes into the bathhouse, and he dances before them. He said to him: Perhaps you have done some good deed? He told him that once a Jewish woman came to him wishing to hire herself out for prostitution, and he saw that she was weeping. He said to her: Why are you weeping? She said to him that her husband was imprisoned, and therefore she wished to hire herself out for prostitution in order to redeem her husband with the money. When he heard this, he took all his household vessels, sold them, and gave her the proceeds to redeem her husband, so that she would not need to engage in prostitution. Then Rabbi Abbahu said to him: You are worthy to pray for rain. And so it was.

notes.text: Hyman summarizes four daily transgressions and the sale of household possessions. The named Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Taanit1:4 text lists five, including playing an instrument, and specifies a bed and bedding. The English preserves Hyman’s account rather than harmonizing its number and details.

The inspected Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 1:4 gives five daily offenses, including playing an instrument, and the sale of a bed and bedding. Hyman gives four offenses and household vessels. His account is retained without silently changing its count or narrative details to match the consulted witness.
